sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: h10 (notes/hooks.md), one publisher named by two citers and not by the third, whose link sits in another submission; same mechanism as h9/i05, which failed its quick test (the easier solver made that link). Target medium (user, 2026-10-13: no Easy slot, "target medium and high"; page: Hard 0/3, Medium 1/2). Quick test: i06 survived (user, 2026-10-14: "i05 failed i06 survived", no panel). Measured platform result pending.
- Dependency plan: D06 line 169 and footnote 3 (line 183) give AFPA's source and name the handbook as Hort Innovation's; D09 line 51 with footnote 2 (line 58) gives AUSVEG's Hort Innovation figure; D13 line 10 gives Fruit Producers SA's source by title only. Three names; D06 is both a member and the link for D13.
- Universe: every submission's stated figure sources were searched (Hort Innovation, Harvest to Home, statistics, handbook, "Source", "sourced", ABARES, ABS, Dairy Australia; 2026-10-14). Hort Innovation as a source: D06, D09. Its handbook by title: D13. Named without a figure: D11 line 325. Other named sources: D05 Figure 1 (ABARES; Dairy Australia), D10 footnote 3 (Dairy Australia), D09 footnote 4 (Australian Bureau of Statistics), D04 (ACMF), D03 (IBISWorld; Hunt Export Advice), D07 (IBISWorld; Wine Australia). Farm-gate figures with no stated source: D09 line 21, D08, D14; they are not counted because no source is named.
- Necessity: D06 is the only document naming Hort Innovation as the handbook's publisher and the only source of AFPA as a member; without it the answer is AUSVEG (and Fruit Producers SA only through outside knowledge). D09 is the only source of AUSVEG's Hort Innovation citation; without it, AUSVEG drops out. D13 is the only source of Fruit Producers SA's citation; without it, two names. D11 supplies the decoy only: removing it leaves the gold unchanged; it is ticked because Step 5 names it (reviewers have returned questions whose steps name unticked documents).
- Selected-lever checks: which-items decoy named and failed (Fresh Markets Australia, D11 line 325, names Hort Innovation without citing its figures). Wrong lists recomputed: link not made, two names (Australian Fresh Produce Alliance, AUSVEG); decoy added, four names (adds Fresh Markets Australia); both slips, three names with the wrong third (Australian Fresh Produce Alliance, AUSVEG, Fresh Markets Australia).
- Targeted failure modes: Linking across documents / Wrong members in a list: the two-name answer when D13's title is not linked to D06's publisher. Declared as the answer the easiest reading gives. How the easier solver failed in the quick test is not known (no panel). The decoy route (adding Fresh Markets Australia) is not declared: no fitting trap in the form's list and no observed attempt. To be matched to the wrong answers the first difficulty run shows, before Submit.
- Calculation verification: not applicable (no arithmetic, no dates). Order checked by script: case-insensitive alphabetical, "Australian Fresh Produce Alliance", "AUSVEG", "Fruit Producers SA".
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: searching "Hort Innovation" lands on D06 lines 169, 183, 184, D09 line 58 and D11 line 325; it never lands on D13. Searching "Statistics" or "Horticultur" lands on D13 line 10 and D06. The bundle overview names neither Hort Innovation nor the handbook. Shortest route: the two named citations, then D06's handbook title matched to D13's source note.
- Precision/readings: (1) a strict reader may hold that "Australian Horticultural Statistics 2022/2023" (D13) and "Australian Horticulture Statistics Handbook 2022/23" (D06) are not shown to be one publication; same subject, same year, near-identical title. The reading stays possible; the form's "One defensible answer" check and the strongest solver's attempts will show whether it is taken. (2) "cite figures published by" read as naming Hort Innovation anywhere: adds Fresh Markets Australia; the question says "cite figures", and D11 cites none. (3) A submitter's unsourced farm-gate figure credited to Hort Innovation from outside knowledge: no document says so. (4) AFPA's footnote 4 ("Contribution of Australian horticulture industry – Hort Innovation") is a second Hort Innovation source for the same member; it does not change the list.
- Completeness: complete capture, no source gaps. All fifteen documents are now read in full: nine by the author, the remaining ranges of D02, D04, D06, D09, D10 and D11 by four mapping agents (notes/map-D02.md, map-D04.md, map-D06.md, map-D09.md, map-D10.md, map-D11.md), with the author re-reading every quoted passage.
- Style/set review: 15 words, one ask, a three-name list in a stated order with the empty case covered by "if any". Shares no evidence or answer path with the failed sketches i01-i05.
- Warnings answered: origin is claude (accurate; the export tool takes user only).

sections.question: Which of these submitters, if any, cite figures published by Hort Innovation? List them alphabetically.
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 5, key facts): the Australian Fresh Produce Alliance says its key facts are "sourced largely from Hort Innovation's Australian Horticulture Statistics Handbook", and its footnote gives that handbook as "Australian Horticulture Statistics Handbook 2022/23 - Hort Innovation". It cites Hort Innovation figures (first component).
Step 2. Source input (Doc 9, executive summary and its footnote): AUSVEG writes "Harvest to Home citing 78 percent of retail fresh vegetables are sold through Coles, Woolworths, and Aldi", and its footnote gives the source as "'Harvest to Home', Hort Innovation". It cites a Hort Innovation figure (second component).
Step 3. Source input (Doc 13, executive summary): Fruit Producers SA gives its growers' "over $150 million in value of production (Source: Australian Horticultural Statistics 2022/2023)". It names no publisher.
Step 4. Join (Doc 5 and Doc 13): Doc 5 says the Australian Horticulture Statistics Handbook for 2022/23 is Hort Innovation's. Fruit Producers SA's source is that publication for the same year, so its figure is also a Hort Innovation figure (third component).
Step 5. Decoy (Doc 11, independent retailers): Fresh Markets Australia names Hort Innovation only to ask that the Government "influence or mandate Hort Innovation to allocate fruit and vegetable levies". It cites no Hort Innovation figure, so it is left out. No other submission names Hort Innovation, Harvest to Home or the horticulture statistics handbook as a source.
Step 6. Final answer (Doc 5, Doc 9 and Doc 13): Australian Fresh Produce Alliance, AUSVEG, Fruit Producers SA.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Linking across documents
How a careless solver fails: Wrong members in a list

Why these are traps: Linking across documents: Doc 13 sources its $150 million to "Australian Horticultural Statistics 2022/2023" and names no publisher; only Doc 5 calls that handbook Hort Innovation's. Searching for Hort Innovation finds Docs 5 and 9 and gives two names; the link adds Fruit Producers SA.
